The problem

You've done the hard part.
The world hasn't caught up.

The product is built

Engineering is no longer the bottleneck. Perception is. The market cannot buy what it has never encountered.

The raise is closed

The category is loud

In crowded markets, the best product rarely wins. The most credible one does.

Omera02 / 32
The old playbook

Attention you pay for is attention the audience discounts.

Paid ads

Rented reach with a disclosure label attached. The moment spend stops, presence stops. Nothing compounds.

Cold outbound

Arrives with no context and no prior signal. The recipient has never seen the name before the pitch lands.

Traditional PR

Slow cycles, opaque outcomes, retainers detached from results. Coverage arrives after the moment has passed.

Each channel asks the audience to trust the brand's own voice. Audiences stopped doing that years ago.

Omera03 / 32
The alternative

Seeding doesn't market.
It builds credibility from the ground up.

Instead of the brand announcing itself, the culture appears to discover it. Content surfaces across independent pages the audience already follows and trusts — in the editorial voice of each page, never the voice of an advertiser.

01

Never branded on first touch

The first frame is never a logo. The story earns interest before the name appears.

02

Staggered, never simultaneous

Releases are sequenced to read as cultural momentum — not a coordinated campaign.

03

Editorial, never advertorial

Every placement reads as discovery. Third-party voice is the credibility mechanism itself.

Omera04 / 32
Organic omnipresence

Every scroll, everywhere —
and none of it reads as an ad.

The goal is not one big placement. It is ambient presence: the same brand met on a meme page, then in a creator clip, then in a comment thread, then in a founder story — each framed as culture, none framed as advertising. The user never feels marketed to. They feel like they keep noticing something.

What paid looks like
Announces itself with a disclosure label — discounted on sight.
Speaks in the brand's voice, interrupting the feed it sits in.
Skipped in under two seconds. Reach without residue.
What omnipresence feels like
Arrives in the native voice of a page the user already trusts.
Consumed as entertainment — watched to the end, screenshotted, shared.
Compounds: each sighting confirms the last. "Why do I keep seeing this?"

Omera06 / 32
The journey to a client

Nobody converts on first contact.

The old rule of thumb was seven touchpoints before a purchase. In today's saturated feeds it is closer to twenty. The question is not whether the journey is long — it is what each touch is worth. An ad impression is a weak touch, discounted the instant it is recognised. A third-party voice is a strong one, because it carries borrowed trust.

TOUCH 1–5 · NOTICING

A meme mention, a creator clip, a comment thread. The name registers without a pitch attached.

TOUCH 6–15 · TRUSTING

Independent voices keep confirming each other. Curiosity turns into a search for the name.

TOUCH 16+ · ACTING

By the time outbound or product lands, it is confirmation — not introduction. This is the 41× effect.

Seeding doesn't shorten the journey by skipping touches. It makes every touch count more.

Omera07 / 32
Why it works
41×

Audiences warmed by earned and third-party coverage convert at up to 41× the rate of cold outreach alone.

When the first touchpoint is discovery rather than a pitch, every subsequent touchpoint inherits that credibility. Outbound stops introducing the brand and starts confirming it.

Seeding is not a substitute for sales or performance channels. It is the layer that makes every other channel convert.
